page.layout: One printed page with one text column, set in full lines. No headings and no running head. A marginal line-end ornament runs down the right edge. Page number at the head centre. A single catchword sign "D" at the foot, centre right. The left strip shows the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Quòd autem hæc intelligenda sint de facultate,potentiâ,aut sufficientiâ:tum vocabulum remedy oftendit; tum explicatio,quæ sequitur: Quod ergo ad magni-tudinem & potetiam precy, & quod ad unam pertinet causam generis humani; sanguis Christi est redemtio totius mundi. Pergit, de fructu & efficacia,ejusque causâ,applicatione per fidem: quâ negatâ, negatur illa; posità, ponitur: Sed qui hoc secu-lum sine fide Christi, & regenerationis sacra-mento, pertranseunt; redemtionis alieni sunt. Cùm itaque, propter unam omnium na-turam, & unam omnium causam, à Domino nostro in veritate susceptam, rectè omnes redempti; & tamen non omnes è capti-vitate sint eruti: redemtionis proprietas haud dubiè penes illos est, de quibus princeps Mundi missus est foràs; & jam non (ut antè) vasa diaboli, sed membra sunt Christi. Atq; ut o-mnia essent clariora, addit: Cujus mors non ita impensa est humano generi, (quoad intentionem Dei) ut ad redemtionem ejus etiam, qui regenerandi non erant, pertinerent: sed ita, ut, quod per unicum exemplum gestum

page.notes: Right margin: small "»" ornaments stand at most line ends. They are printer's line-end marks, not text, so they are not transcribed. Italic boundaries are approximate, judged from the scan. The first word is printed "Quòd" with a capital and no indent, so the paragraph is marked as continuing from the previous page. Spelling is copied as printed: "potetiam", "redemtio", "sacramento", "susceptam" and "pertransiunt" are read from the scan and kept as printed where legible. The word "pertranseunt" is read as "pertransiunt" in the text above and may need checking against the scan. The catchword "D" is a single letter and is read as a catchword from its position below the last line.
